context: Add one in-memory owner (context or signal) for picking state. It survives client-side navigation between entry points and dies with the tab. It never writes ?ids=. sessionStorage carries it across the Pages 404 -> /results/ restore hop only, reusing main.tsx's existing key convention. On load, picked IDs are revalidated through compareRecovery per D5. The seam to compared state is the existing buildCompareUrl. This item is ADDITIVE: existing per-page selection keeps working until rx-ux-18 migrates each route.
description:
Picking state and compared state are different contracts and must not share a query parameter.

Picking: runs a reader has ticked mid-task. Today four ephemeral useState Sets (BenchmarkIndex, PlatformIndex, Query, Compare's builder). Lifetime is the visit. Deliberately NOT shareable.

Compared: the set a comparison renders, carried by /results/compare?ids=. Lifetime is the link. Already shareable and already relied upon.

Merging them - as an earlier revision proposed by URL-backing selection - would make picking shareable and put a global ?ids= into copied links that cannot later be retracted.

Gated on rx-ux-00 D3 (model), D4 (Compare's future) and D5 (revalidation strategy).

anti_patterns.dont: remove any existing page selection in this item
anti_patterns.why: additive migration is what makes each route revertible

anti_patterns.dont: rewrite Compare's ?ids= from the picking owner
anti_patterns.instead: promote to a comparison through buildCompareUrl
anti_patterns.why: Compare's URL canonicalisation has its own recovery rules that must stay authoritative

anti_patterns.dont: serialise picking state into the URL
anti_patterns.instead: keep it in memory with a sessionStorage hop for Pages restore only
anti_patterns.why: a global ?ids= picking contract cannot be retracted once copied into links

preserves.behavior: /results/compare?ids=<one> pins that run and opens the builder (Compare.tsx:184+); ?ids=<a,b> renders a comparison. Both are live contracts (ResultDetail.tsx:266, e2e/routes/compare.spec.ts:58, compare-entrypoints.spec.ts:76).
Compare's ?ids= URL machine is untouched by this item
Compare's recovery rule that a multi-selection URL stays multi after a one-result recovery, so it does not collapse into the single-result builder (Compare.tsx:331-350).
MAX_COMPARE_SELECTIONS as the single cap constant
